title: Whose shell is it?
hook: Some crabs carry protection they did not grow.

knows: A shell can be a separate object from the animal inside.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a borrowed snail shell from a crab’s own exoskeleton.

misconception: A hermit crab’s borrowed shell is its own body covering.
objective: Distinguish a borrowed snail shell from a crab’s own exoskeleton.

claims.text: Some crabs carry protection they did not grow. A hermit crab occupies an empty snail shell. Which description fits the shell? The schematic hermit crab occupies an empty shell originally made by a snail. The borrowed shell is distinct from the crab’s own exoskeleton and can protect its abdomen; individual crabs may change shells as they grow.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A hermit crab moves from one empty snail shell into another. Which part is borrowed? The crab occupies an external shell made by another animal.
